name: Invalid string escape
description: Flags an unsupported C-like escape such as \r inside a string literal; the Papyrus compiler only translates \n, \t, \\ and \", which are never flagged.
definition: Flags, as a `[warning]`, a string literal that contains the C-like escape sequence `\r`. The Papyrus compiler translates exactly four escapes in string literals — `\n` (newline), `\t` (tab), `\\` (backslash) and `\"` (double quote) — as verified for Skyrim by compiling a probe script and inspecting the `.pex` string table (#1761); these are never reported. `\r` is not a supported escape, so authors coming from C/JavaScript/Python who write `"Line\r"` expecting a carriage return do not get one. Only `\r` is checked, to avoid noise from intentional Windows-style paths that contain other backslash-letter pairs (`"C:\Games"`). The diagnostic names the escape that was found. Not auto-fixable: the author's intent cannot be inferred safely.
